title: AI Agent 生态与社区创造周报

signals.title: VibeGamesStudio models continuous software production as an agent organization
signals.summary: VibeGamesStudio assigns scheduled creative, implementation, improvement, code-health, QA, sound, and release work to distinct agents around a growing playable game catalog. The durable signal is the clock, bounded role contracts, artifact handoffs, and independent gate—not the creator's unverified zero-human framing.
signals.evidence_level: Real Product / Live Experiment + Creator Claim

signals.title: Ordewell makes the implementation plan an editable pre-execution artifact
signals.summary: Ordewell uses a read-only planner to expose tasks, dependencies, runners, models, reasoning modes, and execution modes before independent coding sessions begin. This moves human correction to a low-side-effect point, while its completion marker remains protocol acknowledgement rather than proof that the requested outcome is correct.

signals.title: SuperDev extends coding-agent context from the repository into the live runtime
signals.summary: SuperDev lets coding agents inspect processes, ports, logs, debugger state, browser behavior, and network activity, then places runtime writes behind operation-bound approval tokens and local audit. The reported zombie-server failure shows why restart claims need PID and start-time evidence before an agent changes otherwise-correct code.

signals.title: AI Guard converts recurring agent-code failures into deterministic CI gates
signals.summary: AI Guard encodes recurring empty-catch, floating-promise, unsafe-async, placeholder-secret, missing-auth, and dynamic-evaluation failures as ESLint, CLI, SARIF, and pull-request checks. Its reported shift toward lower false-positive rates and easier adoption makes guardrail noise and ongoing enablement part of reliability design.
signals.evidence_level: Open Source Project / Reproducible Engineering Practice

signals.title: Bookery illustrates the human shift toward product and architecture work
signals.summary: Bookery is presented as a sustained open-source product in which the creator retains feature specification, architecture, coherence, and acceptance while delegating nearly all implementation to Claude Code. The code-authorship percentage remains a creator claim; the transferable signal is the redistribution of responsibility rather than removal of human work.
signals.evidence_level: Real Open Source Product + Creator Claim

signals.title: TurnLens makes the agent turn a practical telemetry unit
signals.summary: TurnLens parses local Claude Code and Codex JSONL transcripts to attribute tokens, tool calls, model use, completion state, and API-equivalent cost to individual turns. Its disclosed sub-agent undercount, duplicate-message, cache-pricing, and subscription-billing limitations show why transcript semantics must accompany agent cost figures.

signals.title: Claude Tag turns a shared team channel into an agent workspace
signals.summary: Claude Tag places shared channel context, administrator-authorized tools, asynchronous thread work, steering, and follow-up in the same team conversation. This makes public organizational context—not a private copied prompt—the workspace boundary, while Anthropic's internal adoption claims remain first-party evidence.

signals.title: CopilotKit Channels abstracts channel-native agent integration
signals.summary: CopilotKit Channels provides adapters and channel-native interaction primitives for bringing existing agents into team communication surfaces, including streaming, context, approval, and UI. Together with vendor-managed channel agents, it makes the channel-native agent a trackable product form rather than a one-off bot integration.

patterns.title: Agent as Organization
patterns.summary: Agents are assigned roles, schedules, bounded jobs, durable artifacts, handoffs, and independent gates inside a continuing production loop.
patterns.outlook: Early but strong signal. Durable differentiation is more likely to come from policy, QA, and cross-run state than from persona count.

patterns.title: Human as Product/Architecture Layer
patterns.summary: Humans retain problem selection, product scope, architecture, coherence, and acceptance while agents take a larger share of implementation and iteration.
patterns.outlook: High-probability long-term pattern, especially for one-person teams with strong engineering judgment.

patterns.title: Plan as First-class Artifact
patterns.summary: Task graphs, dependencies, models, and execution choices become visible and editable before code-changing sessions begin.
patterns.outlook: Strong signal and a comparatively low-complexity way to reduce expensive rework on long-running tasks.

patterns.title: Agent Sidecar Infrastructure
patterns.summary: Runtime sensors, deterministic quality gates, and turn-level telemetry are emerging around coding agents to supply truth, constraints, and evidence that the model cannot safely self-attest.
patterns.outlook: The strongest pattern to continue tracking because evidence, guardrails, and telemetry become more important as agent autonomy increases.

ideas.title: Evidence-backed skill maturity
ideas.summary: Assess skill maturity through real runs, repository spread, successful outcomes, human overrides, false-positive workflow triggers, known failure modes, and adoption cost. Observe this evidence first rather than expanding the registry schema immediately.
